entry.title: Russian extremist group denies sending hoax bomb threats
entry.summary: Scores of flights across Europe have received bomb threats this week, but no explosives have been found so far.

entry.title: Some media firms evacuated after hoax bomb threats
entry.summary: Gardaí say they are "aware of a threat made against media organisations here and in Europe".

entry.title: Man investigated for leaving 17-year-old on Germany's highest mountain
entry.summary: The teenager was eventually rescued on Zugspitze and has since been discharged from hospital.

entry.title: Self-styled 'king of Germany' goes on trial accused of heading criminal group
entry.summary: Peter Fitzek is a member of a banned Reichsbürger group that sought to set up the "Kingdom of Germany" (KRD).

entry.title: Two dead after bus crashes in France, officials say
entry.summary: One child and one young adult were killed in the crash, local authorities say, with more injured.

entry.title: A wildfire killed their loved ones in Spain. These British families demand to know why
entry.summary: Nine British nationals were among the 15 people who died when fire ripped through the village of Bédar this summer.

entry.title: Pope begins lengthy trip to Latin America weeks after lung cancer surgery
entry.summary: Pope Leo, who had part of a lung removed last month, will visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru.

entry.title: Melania Trump calls for lasting Ukraine truce as she hosts Russian and Ukrainian officials
entry.summary: The US first lady was credited by all for playing a key though unspecified role in the ceasefire.

entry.title: Who could be behind hoax bomb threats to European air travel?
entry.summary: There is no hard evidence so far linking airline bomb threats to Russia, Iran or any proxy groups.

entry.title: Dutch launch shows smugglers are adapting, says MP
entry.summary: Dover MP Mike Tapp says smugglers will find new launch locations and methods due to disruptions.

entry.title: French protests see numbers surge as unions join strikes over high cost of living
entry.summary: The interior ministry estimates 600,000 people joined protests across France, while the unions say the number was far higher.

entry.title: Hoax bomb threats target European airlines and airports for second time in a week
entry.summary: At least 21 flights across Europe are affected in what the UK government calls a "malicious hoax threat".

entry.title: Eight killed in series of shootings in western Turkey
entry.summary: Victims are found in several locations in three separate vehicles, according to local reports.

entry.title: Italian chef fired after refusing to put pineapple on pizza
entry.summary: He had told his employer, an Australian restaurant, that pineapple on pizza was "offensive" to Italian culture.

entry.title: Secret police files released in Hungary, 37 years after fall of communism
entry.summary: Critics say the move comes too late, that the files themselves are incomplete, and the move risks sowing division and causing unnecessary anguish.

entry.title: Brigitte Bardot inheritance row deepens after private letter to partner leaked
entry.summary: In the letter, the late French actress says her partner Bernard de Chiara was "incapable" of giving "support, a tenderness, a presence".

entry.title: How the downfall of Serbia's Vučiċ mirrored that of Hungary's Orbán
entry.summary: Defeat for Serbia's Aleksandar Vučiċ in last weekend's vote was a carbon copy of Viktor Orbán's fall in Hungary.

entry.title: Emotional reunions with loved ones for Oleshky evacuees
entry.summary: The BBC's Dan Johnson travelled to the northern Ukrainian border with Belarus after evacuated Oleshky residents arrived in buses and ambulances following a temporary ceasefire.

entry.title: Why are new strikes and protests taking place in France?
entry.summary: More than 250,000 people had taken to the streets in almost 70 towns and cities by Thursday afternoon, and that was "just the start", the CGT union said.

entry.title: Kremlin: 'Trump will continue his foreign policy'
entry.summary: Kremlin spokesman responds to midterm results

entry.title: Was an Italian chef really fired over refusal to put pineapple on pizza?
entry.summary: The chef had stated that putting pineapple on pizza was "offensive to his culture".

entry.title: Ryanair passenger says bomb threat was 'traumatic'
entry.summary: Sarah Jones says passengers had to wait in a hangar for three hours after landing at Murcia in Spain.

entry.title: 'All this food is now useless': Piles of rubbish after shop freezers hit by cyber-attack
entry.summary: Dozens of supermarkets in seven European countries dumped huge quantities of food after refrigerators and freezers were targeted in a cyber-attack.
